title: Frontend: Shortest Distance from Source (BFS)
businessContext: Build and verify the core behavior behind Shortest Distance from Source (BFS). This independently authored exercise has a bounded, explicit contract. Injected clock, network, random, or worker models are identified in the contract; they do not claim production service guarantees.
problemStatement: Implement solution({count,edges,source}). In a valid undirected unweighted graph, return edge-count distances or null for unreachable vertices. Use a queue with a head index.
constraints: Define solution(input) in plain JavaScript. Return the documented JSON-compatible value or throw the documented validation error. Each case receives a fresh input.
Preserve identity, ordering, boundary behavior, and error messages stated in the contract. Passing fixtures verifies this contract, not every production concern.
candidateTasks: Implement the documented behavior without hard-coding fixture answers.
Run the full suite, investigate boundary failures, and explain the follow-up variation.
hints: Write down the state or algorithmic invariant, and trace the smallest boundary case before coding.
Use a queue, initialize the source distance to zero, and mark vertices when enqueued so each vertex enters once.
alternativeApproaches: Return parent links for path reconstruction and define deterministic tie-breaking among equally short paths.
commonMistakes: Ignoring contract boundaries such as: Disconnected node; self-loop; multiple equal paths.
Treating a local deterministic model as proof of durable storage, authorization, distributed coordination, or physical-world guarantees.
